patient_identity.statement: The only new patient is a boy assessed at5years,matching the selected packet male sex,ageP5Y and White–Sutton syndrome. General WHSUS/SMS descriptions and literature patients are kept separate from this child.

genotype.statement: Source reports NM_015100.3:c.3631C>T,p.Arg1211*,matching packet coding change and protein stop. Packet NM_015100.4,GRCh38chr1:g.151405404G>A and explicit heterozygous state are not independently established by the printed sequence data;no raw chromatogram or allelic count supplied.

evidence.locator: Clinical Reportp1794 final paragraph;Figure1cp1792 red p.Arg1211* label.

limitations: Transcript version/assembly conversion not independently normalized;heterozygosity is not explicitly documented with raw genotype evidence.

segregation.statement: The source explicitly reports a de novo variant identified by family-based whole-exome sequencing,after negative karyotype/array-CGH and unremarkable family history. This supports reported de novo status;individual parental calls/validation and parentage details are not printed.

evidence.locator: Clinical Reportp1794 final paragraph;Figure1cp1792 red p.Arg1211* label.

limitations: Reported family-based evidence accepted as source claim;independent raw-parental verification unavailable.

phase.statement: One POGZ variant is reported;no paired variants needing cis/trans adjudication. No independent phase data are supplied.

evidence.locator: Clinical Reportp1794 final paragraph;Figure1cp1792 red p.Arg1211* label.

limitations: Single-allele report;not a phase-confirmed multi-variant genotype.

causal_confidence.statement: Authors attribute the child’s White–Sutton phenotype to the novel de novo nonsense variant and predict truncation/disrupted DDE-domain activity. The source states sequencing excluded other significant phenotype-related variants,but provides no functional validation or complete raw data. This is source correspondence,not independent clinical truth.

evidence.locator: Clinical Reportp1794 final paragraph;Figure1cp1792 red p.Arg1211* label. Discussionp1794.

limitations: Predicted molecular effect and authors’ interpretation,not independently validated pathogenicity.

phenotype_completeness.statement: All26packet features compared individually. Packet omits explicit aortic bicuspid valve/mild ascending-aortic dilation,sleep–wake disturbance,obesity,hepatomegaly,drooling,abnormal cochleo-stapedial reflexes and several distinctive behavioral observations. Some packet facial/motor/MRI assertions are not individually reported;general SMS/WHSUS descriptions were not transferred.
limitations: Packet is neither exhaustive nor fully supported at exact HPO granularity;source has internal table/caption discrepancies recorded separately.

assessment.statement: Source reports NM_015100.3:c.3631C>T,p.Arg1211*,matching packet coding change and protein stop. Packet NM_015100.4,GRCh38chr1:g.151405404G>A and explicit heterozygous state are not independently established by the printed sequence data;no raw chromatogram or allelic count supplied.

evidence.locator: Clinical Reportp1794 final paragraph;Figure1cp1792 red p.Arg1211* label.

limitations: Transcript version/assembly conversion not independently normalized;heterozygosity is not explicitly documented with raw genotype evidence.

assessment.statement: Mild macroglossia explicitly reportedp1792 and reiteratedp1794.
Prognathism explicitly described in this childp1792;Figure1a provides associated clinical views.
Patient description states thin upper lip with thick lower vermilionp1792.
Low-set ears occurs in the general SMS descriptionp1794,not this child’s specific clinical findings. Unmeasured photographs are insufficient to establish exact ear position.
limitations: Syndrome-level description cannot establish individual finding.

assessment.statement: Hypertelorism is listed among general WHSUS features in the Introduction,not documented for the new child in the clinical report.
limitations: No individual measurement or explicit finding;no diagnosis inferred from photographs.

assessment.statement: Astigmatism explicitly reportedp1794.
The patient text reports broad toes but does not state broad fingers. Figure1a hand photo and normal radiograph do not provide a measured finger-width diagnosis.
limitations: Broad toes cannot be transferred to fingers;no explicit hand-width assessment.

assessment.statement: Broad toes explicitly reportedp1794 and foot photograph present inFigure1a.
Brachycephaly explicitly describedp1792.
Joint hyperlaxity explicitly reportedp1794,supporting joint hypermobility.
Height126cm above97thcentilep1792 andTable1 explicitly0/1(tall) support exclusion of short stature atage5.
Source describes a wide nasal ridge,not a depressed nasal bridge. The latter is not established by broadness alone.
limitations: Distinct shape descriptors;no explicit depressed-bridge finding.

assessment.statement: Broad nasal tip explicitly reportedp1792.
Bulbous nose with broad tip is explicitly describedp1792 and may support a broad shape resemblance;the precise pear-shaped term is not used.
limitations: Exact HPO shape equivalence not established.

assessment.statement: Midface hypoplasia/flat midface occurs in general WHSUS/SMS descriptions;the child-specific description does not establish midface retrusion.
limitations: General syndrome description and unmeasured photograph are insufficient for exact individual feature.

assessment.statement: MRI explicitly reports hypoplasia of the inferior cerebellar vermisp1794,supporting cerebellar hypoplasia at this specified regional extent.
MRI describes wide communication between the fourth ventricle and pericerebellar fluid spaces,not ventricular enlargement. Ventriculomegaly is not explicitly established.
limitations: Communication with fluid spaces is not equivalent to enlarged ventricles.

assessment.statement: Discussion explicitly identifies DD/ID as the proband’s core phenotype;multiple developmental domains are affected in the clinical report.
Sitting at32weeks,walking alone at18months and abnormal motor coordination are reportedp1792,in the context of DD. Exact gross-motor-delay diagnosis/severity is not separately stated.
limitations: Milestone/coordination report supports a qualified mapping rather than precise domain measurement.

assessment.statement: Abnormal motor coordination is reported,but fine-motor milestones or an explicit fine-motor-delay assessment are not supplied.
limitations: General motor difficulty cannot establish this specific developmental domain.

assessment.statement: Atage5 speech is limited to a few words and no full phrases;language is explicitly severely impairedp1794.

Authors describe borderline ID with IQ74p1792 and DD/ID inTable1/Discussion. The packet broad ID label corresponds to the authors’ wording,but adaptive-function assessment and a definite ID threshold are not supplied.
limitations: Borderline IQ/combined DD-ID reporting does not independently confirm a categorical ID diagnosis.

assessment.statement: Autism with restricted interests and refusal of changes explicitly reportedp1792;present-patient ASD1/1 inTable1.
Anxiety explicitly reportedp1794,with agoraphobia also described.

Attention deficit is reportedp1792,but no formal ADHD diagnosis or individual hyperactivity assessment is supplied. Table1 combines behavioral alterations/stereotypies/hyperactivity in a single disjunctive row.
limitations: Combined row positivity cannot establish each diagnosis in its heading.

assessment.statement: Dysphagia and drooling reportedp1794 and present-patient GI/feeding-problems1/1 inTable1 support feeding difficulty.
